strategies.overview: With its blisteringly fast Speed and a deadly STAB combination, Sneasel carves a place for itself in ZU as a powerful wallbreaker and cleaner. STAB Knock Off makes Sneasel excellent at forcing progress, especially since the primary Knock Off absorber, Dipplin, fears its Ice-type attacks, and it outruns many already fast threats like Charizard and Virizion. However, Sneasel's paper-thin defenses mean it crumples to most strong neutral attacks and, combined with its many weaknesses, give it near to no defensive utility outside of switching into Psychic-type attacks. Sneasel also can be left wanting in power and struggles to break past walls like Regirock and Orthworm. Choice Band sets don't have this problem but are vulnerable to entry hazards and very prediction reliant. Lastly, Sneasel is incredibly vulnerable to getting revenge killed by most Choice Scarf users in the tier, like Primeape, Sneasel-Hisui, and Typhlosion, as well as priority attacks such as Mach Punch from Hitmontop.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Sneasel has no other options.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Sneasel greatly fears Fighting-types like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel. Most of them don't enjoy switching in on Sneasel's attacks, however, though Poliwrath resists Sneasel's STAB moves and doesn't take much damage from Low Kick.

Choice Scarf Users: Sneasel's lack of bulk means that Choice Scarf users have an easy time outspeeding it and taking it out. All of Hisuian Sneasel, Primeape, and Mesprit can revenge kill Sneasel with ease.

Physical Walls: Physically bulky Pokemon like Regirock, Orthworm, and Weezing don't fear much from Sneasel and can force it out with status conditions or super effective attacks. However, since all three of them lack reliable recovery, and the former two hate losing Leftovers, Sneasel can slowly wear them down over a longer game. Glastrier also can take Sneasel on but hates losing its Heavy-Duty Boots. All of them except Weezing also must be wary of Low Kick.

movesets.name: Fast Attacker
movesets.description:
Ice Shard lets Sneasel pick off weakened foes and faster attackers like Whimsicott and Jolteon as well as dance around priority like Mach Punch from Hitmonchan. Swords Dance lets Sneasel pick up OHKOs on Charizard and Dipplin and gives it an easier time cleaning up weakened teams, while Low Kick lets it threaten Orthworm, Regirock, and Glastrier more immediately. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Sneasel come in without taking damage from entry hazards, allowing it to come in many times over the course of a game. Tera Ice boosts Triple Axel and Ice Shard's power immensely, netting a 2HKO on Regirock and Weezing at +2, but does nothing to help Sneasel's terrible defensive typing. Tera Ghost flips Sneasel's Fighting weakness into an immunity, letting it blank Close Combat from revenge killers like Choice Scarf Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel.

Sneasel's powerful Knock Off makes it an excellent pick on entry hazard stacking teams where teammates such as Sandslash and Orthworm help Sneasel push past bulkier foes like Magneton and Poliwrath. Sneasel struggles to break past physically bulky foes like Regirock, Orthworm, and Weezing, so teammates that share these checks like Charizard, Mesprit, and Virizion, respectively, can team up to wear down said walls. Poliwrath notably takes little damage from Sneasel's STAB attacks, so teammates that handle it like Whimsicott and Venusaur are quite helpful. Physical wallbreakers like Lycanroc and Swords Dance Charizard also help wear walls down so Sneasel can sweep. Fighting-types like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel threaten Sneasel immensely, so defensive fallbacks like Weezing make for great teammates. Other defensive teammates such as Venusaur and Poliwrath help make up for Sneasel's lack of defenses, dealing with threats like Whimsicott and Typhlosion for it. As Sneasel struggles to switch in directly, pivots like Jolteon, Primeape, and Whimsicott are all helpful in assisting Sneasel to hit the field safely. On more offensive teams, it can pair up with other setup sweepers like Toxicroak and Mesprit to overwhelm the opposing team.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Sneasel has very strong STAB moves and a great Speed tier to spam them. A Choice Band gives Sneasel the immediate raw power to make quick offensive progress against bulky Pokemon like Orthworm and Regirock. Choice Band also makes Sneasel a more reliable revenge killer to offensive threats like Charizard, Nasty Plot Mesprit, and Virizion. Low Kick is Sneasel's strongest move against physically bulky Pokemon like Glastrier, Regirock, and Orthworm, which take neutral or resisted damage from its STAB moves, but its limited coverage and variable power make it a difficult option to lock into. Tera Ice cranks up the power of Sneasel's strongest STAB move to ice out bulkier Pokemon such as Tera Fairy Nasty Plot Mesprit and Weezing. Tera Ice also boosts Sneasel's priority to more effectively pick off Jolteon and Whimsicott.

Choice Band Sneasel has great immediate damage output, quickly cutting through teams with Triple Axel and making progress with Knock Off. Choice Band Sneasel's ability to lure in and remove Leftovers from Regirock makes it a great enabler to offensive Pokemon that struggle against it such as Charizard and Minior, and it functions similarly against Orthworm to support Mesprit and Whimsicott. Knock Off removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes creates excellent synergy with entry hazard setting Pokemon such as Sandslash and Orthworm. Choice Band Sneasel is vulnerable to being worn down by entry hazards, particularly Stealth Rock, so hazard removers like Sandslash and Lurantis are critical to maximizing Sneasel's offensive presence. Defensive pivots like Eelektross and Mesprit can bring Sneasel in safely in spite of its poor bulk and vulnerable defensive typing. While Sneasel resists Shadow Sneak and Sucker Punch from foes like Muk and Hitmontop, its frailty leaves it prone to strong and super effective priority users; Sandaconda and Weezing can check Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel for Sneasel. Choice Band Sneasel is fast but still struggles with revenge killers like Primeape, Choice Specs, and Choice Scarf Typhlosion, which can be respectively handled by teammates like Orthworm, Weezing, and Regirock.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Sneasel is an effective Swords Dance sweeper in PU thanks to its incredible STAB combination alongside a decent Attack stat, which both let it hit threats such as Espeon, Hisuian Decidueye, and Delphox, and a great Speed tier that allows it to outspeed all of the previously mentioned Pokemon. With Knock Off, Sneasel can hinder common switch-ins such as Paldean Tauros-F and Hariyama by removing their items. Ice Shard is useful to pick off Choice Scarf users such as Florges and Pawmot while also stopping setup sweepers like Oricorio-F and Jolteon. While Heavy-Duty Boots is generally preferred due to Sneasel's Stealth Rock weakness, Life Orb is an option on some hyper offense teams to allow Sneasel to ensure rolls such as OHKOing Calm Mind Florges and Rhydon at +2. Inner Focus is chosen as Sneasel's ability, as the immunity to Fake Out and Intimidate is helpful against Ambipom, Arcanine, and Paldean Tauros-F. In terms of Tera type, Tera Ice boosts the power of Triple Axel to nuclear levels, allowing Sneasel to OHKO Mudsdale after a Swords Dance and 2HKO even Pokemon that resist Ice-type moves, like Arcanine and Qwilfish. It also boosts Ice Shard to make Sneasel a more reliable revenge killer. Alternatively, Tera Ghost benefits Sneasel defensively by giving it immunity to priority such as Arcanine's Extreme Speed and Pawmot's Mach Punch while allowing it to set up in the face of Pokemon that would otherwise threaten it out, like the aforementioned Pawmot and Choice item-locked Paldean Tauros-F.

Sneasel is used almost exclusively on offense and hyper offense teams as a secondary sweeper and cleaner and is usually paired with another sweeper like Arcanine or Espeon to help it in its sweep. Espeon's Magic Bounce also comes in handy if Sneasel is running Life Orb. Sneasel's ability to rip holes through common Ground- and Grass-types like Mudsdale, Rhydon, and Venusaur helps enable teammates such as Rotom-H, Salazzle, and Golurk to more easily steamroll an opposing team. Since Sneasel's poor defenses keep it from coming in safely, offensive pivots that can bring it onto the battlefield like Jolteon, Ambipom, and Bruxish are excellent teammates. Even after a Swords Dance, Sneasel still needs help chipping walls like Milotic and Terastallized Rhydon so they can be in range of its attacks. As such, Goodra and Delphox are excellent teammates in this role.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Despite its NFE status, Sneasel is a real threat in PU due to it being one of the fastest Pokemon in the tier. When holding Choice Band, Sneasel packs a punch with its relatively high Attack stat and can break through even some of the best walls in the tier such as Venusaur and Amoonguss with Triple Axel. Ice Shard helps Sneasel by KOing low-HP foes such as sweepers like Espeon and Oricorio, or getting damage on faster Pokemon such as Hisuian Electrode and Choice Scarf Zoroark. Low Kick allows Sneasel to hit Steel- and Dark-types such as Alolan Sandslash and Alolan Persian for good damage. Sneasel typically runs Tera Ice to amplify the power of Triple Axel and Ice Shard, making it so that Triple Axel always OHKOes Florges no matter how much bulk it has invested. Tera Dark also benefits Sneasel by removing its weakness to Stealth Rock and Fire-type moves.

Sneasel typically appears on teams ranging from hyper offense to bulky offense, where it acts as a wallbreaker alongside Pokemon such as Paldean Tauros-F and Hoopa. Sneasel benefits these partners by providing chip damage on opposing Pokemon such as Florges and Amoonguss, while also removing their item, making them easier to deal with for the rest of the team. Sneasel likes partners that can deal with Fighting- and Fire-type Pokemon such as Paldean-Tauros-F, Delphox, and Arcanine; such partners include Espeon, Bruxish, and Hisuian Braviary. However, even with a Choice Band, Sneasel still can't muscle through bulkier walls such as Milotic and Qwilfish, so Sneasel enjoys having partners that check them such as Pawmot and Palossand, respectively. When using Sneasel, entry hazard control is imperative, as it cannot function well without it, so having teammates such as Espeon, Tatsugiri and Alolan Sandslash really help Sneasel. Sneasel profits off having other wallbreakers such as Dudunsparce and Arcanine, since it can often struggle to OHKO opposing Pokemon. Since Sneasel is so frail, it really enjoys having teammates that are slow pivots so Sneasel can safely get in to threaten opposing Pokemon such as Florges, Hariyama and Goodra. Some such teammates are Uxie, Milotic, and Frosmoth.
